# Receipt compatibility across engine revisions

A signed local review receipt names the engine revision that produced it (`reviewer_sha`, `reviewer_digest`). Today CI
accepts it only when that is exactly the protected `main` it resolved. `main` moves many times a day, so a receipt
rots within hours and CI repeats a review (about $6 and several minutes) even when the engine change cannot affect what
the review attests. This design lets CI accept a receipt issued under revision X while running revision Y, if and only if
Y itself declares X's review semantics compatible. If CI cannot establish that, it behaves as it does today: the receipt is
ignored and CI reviews.

## Design

**Review-semantics digest.** `src/review-semantics.cjs` hashes every engine file under the same roots as the exact engine
digest (`action.yml`, `src`, `policy`, `bin`, `skills`, `scripts`; tests excluded) *except* the files listed in its
`NEUTRAL` table. Each neutral file has a written reason. A file is semantic by default: a new or renamed file is part of
the meaning until a person lists it as neutral. The table lives in `review-semantics.cjs`, which is itself semantic, so
moving a file into it changes the digest and forces the same decision as editing the file would.

**Compatibility statement.** `policy/review-compatibility.json` is in-tree on protected main:

```json
{"version": 1, "current": "<digest of this tree>", "compatible": ["<older digest>", "..."]}
```

`current` must equal the digest of the tree that contains it. `compatible` lists earlier semantics whose receipts this
tree accepts (at most 64, newest first, never including `current`). The statement is the only source of compatibility.

Two further files exist only to keep the statement in step with the tree, and `acceptor()` never reads them:

- `compat/manifest.json` lists the semantic files (path, executable bits, content hash) the statement was last folded for.
  Its digest must equal `current`. It lets a tool say which semantic files changed since the fold by comparing two file
  lists, with no Git history.
- `compat/declarations/<digest>.json`, one file per pull request, state that a set of semantic files changed (by content
  hash, or deleted) and whether the change is `compatible` or `incompatible`. A declaration is inert until it is folded.

**Receipt.** A receipt additionally signs `reviewer_semantics`, the digest of the engine that issued it. Receipts without
the field behave exactly as before.

**Acceptance.** `verifySignedRecord` keeps every check it has (enrolled key, author, expiry, record binding, repository,
head, base, policy and configuration digests, recomputed decision, passing result). Only when the exact engine comparison
fails, and only in central-source mode, it asks `acceptor()` whether the receipt's `reviewer_semantics` is acceptable.
`acceptor()` reads the statement from the engine checkout that is running, the checkout `identifyEngine` and
`verifyEngine` already bound to the SHA the resolver read from protected `gaulatti/clouseau` `main`. It answers yes only
if the statement parses, `current` equals the digest it computes from that checkout, and the claim is `current` or listed.
Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

Declarations chain: after A to B and B to C were both declared compatible, A's receipts are accepted under C. When two pull
requests are folded together, their combined step is compatible only if both declared `compatible`. If a series of small
changes could add up to a different review, declare the last one incompatible. After about 50 further `compatible` folds the
64-entry cap drops the oldest digests and receipts issued under them are ignored again.

Two pull requests that edit the **same** semantic file are the one case that still needs a second declaration: Git may merge
the text, but the merged content then matches neither declaration, so `verify` fails until one author deletes their
declaration and declares again. That is the safe direction.

## Why the list cannot go stale silently (the enforcement argument)

The risk is a semantic change that nobody declared, so that CI accepts a receipt from a weaker or different review. The
argument has four steps.

1. The digest is a function of the bytes of the semantic files, so any semantic change changes it. Reverting restores the
   old digest, which is sound because the bytes are identical.
2. The statement is rejected unless `current` equals the digest of its own tree (`acceptor()`; unchanged by the declare
   and fold flow). The engine's required `verify` job asserts that every semantic file that differs from the manifest is
   covered by exactly one valid declaration, so a change to a semantic file cannot merge without a visible
   `--compatible` or `--incompatible` decision bound to that file's content. Between the merge and the fold, `current`
   no longer equals the digest of the tree, so `acceptor()` answers no to everything: receipts are ignored and CI reviews.
   Only the fold turns a decision into a statement, and it applies the same checks as `verify`.
3. Default-semantic classification closes the "unclassified file" gap: adding a file, renaming one or editing the neutral
   table all change the digest. Listing a file as neutral requires a reason, and the test fails if semantic code loads or
   names any neutral file (apart from `src/cli-usage.cjs`, marked presentation), so a dependency cannot be mislabelled
   neutral by accident.
4. The statement, the manifest, the declarations, the module, the test and every other file under `src/`, `policy/`,
   `compat/`, `scripts/`, `bin/` and `skills/` are protected review controls (`sensitive_paths`). A change to them already needs the owner's exact-revision confirmation.
   The enforcement is a ratchet that makes the owner's compatibility decision unavoidable and visible, not a technical lock
   against an owner who approves a wrong declaration.

There is deliberately a window between a merge and its fold in which main's statement is stale. It is safe because
`acceptor()` refuses everything then (receipts are ignored and CI reviews), and it is short: the fold follows the merge's
review workflow, any push that touches `compat/declarations/`, and a half-hourly schedule. If a fold cannot run or fails,
the window stays open and CI keeps reviewing; nothing is ever accepted on the strength of an unfolded declaration.

## Threat analysis

Attacker: the holder of an enrolled signing key, who is also the PR author, or the PR author alone.

| Attempt | Outcome |
| --- | --- |
| Receipt claims a `reviewer_semantics` that the running engine does not list | Ignored (`engine`); CI reviews |
| Receipt or PR supplies its own statement or digest | There is no input path: the statement is read only from the resolved protected engine checkout |
| PR edits `policy/review-compatibility.json` in the consumer or engine repository | The consumer's checkout is never read; in the engine repository CI runs the frozen protected main, not the PR |
| PR adds a declaration, or edits the manifest, to hide or reclassify a semantic change | Declarations are inert to `acceptor()`. `verify` binds each to the content hash of the files it names, and a manifest that does not hash to `current` fails; both are protected paths |
| PR changes a semantic file and no declaration covers it | `verify` fails; the PR cannot merge |
| A declaration is run through the fold from a pull request or a fork | The fold runs only on `gaulatti/clouseau` `refs/heads/main`, from a main-only checkout, and refuses elsewhere |
| Weak engine fork signs a receipt naming a real compatible digest | Same trust as today: an enrolled key already vouches for `reviewer_sha`/`reviewer_digest`, which CI cannot re-derive from the receipt. Not widened; see residual risks |
| Receipt from an unlisted or retired semantics, or from a fixed-digest (non central-source) trust | Ignored; fixed-digest trust never uses this path |
| Tampering with `reviewer_semantics` after signing | Breaks the signature |
| Replaying a compatible receipt on another head, base, repository, author, policy or configuration | All existing bindings still apply |
| Statement unreadable, malformed, stale, or the digest cannot be computed (symlink, missing file) | `acceptor()` answers no; receipt ignored |

## Failure modes

| Condition | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Receipt has no `reviewer_semantics` | Today's behaviour: exact engine match or ignored |
| Old CI engine meets a receipt with the new field | Unknown field: `malformed`, ignored (fail closed) |
| Statement stale after a semantic change | Undeclared: engine test fails. Declared and merged but not yet folded: receipts are ignored until the fold |
| Declarations inconsistent with the tree, or fold cannot push | Fold changes nothing and fails; receipts stay ignored |
| Semantics digest unknown to the statement | Ignored |
| More than 64 digests listed | Statement malformed, receipts ignored |
| Receipt older than 48 hours | Expired by the existing rule, whatever the statement lists |

## Rollout

Consumers change nothing: their workflows already resolve protected main, and the receipt format only gains an optional
signed field. The work lands as independent pull requests that change no behaviour until the last one:

1. Semantics digest, statement, maintainer tool and enforcement test (this document). Nothing calls them.
2. Receipt format: an optional signed `reviewer_semantics`, accepted by the verifier and issued when a caller supplies it,
   and an optional acceptance hook consulted only after an exact engine mismatch. No caller passes either.
3. Integrator: local review supplies the digest when it issues a receipt, and the verifier's hook defaults to
   `acceptor()`. Receipts issued from that point carry the field; receipts of the preceding revisions are not retrofitted
   and stay governed by exact match. To roll back, make the hook default `null` again; no receipt or statement needs to
   change.

Each pull request that changes semantic files declares the change (`declare`); none of them edits the statement.

## Residual risks

- The receipt's engine claim is not independently re-derived. A signer with an enrolled key could claim a compatible
  digest while running modified code. This is the existing trust in the enrolled signer; a later hardening can fetch the
  claimed revision and recompute its semantics digest.
- Chained declarations can hide a cumulative change (see above).
- A wrong `--compatible` is a human error the system makes visible but cannot detect.
- The neutral table is conservative; moving more files into it (with a reason) reduces how often a declaration is needed.
- The fold and the maintainer tool (`src/review-compatibility-cli.cjs`, `scripts/review-compatibility`) are receipt-neutral, as `bump`
  always was, so editing them does not change the digest; they are protected review controls and `src/review-compatibility-cli.test.cjs`
  pins their behaviour. `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml` is pinned by `.github/tests/compat-fold.test.mjs` (permissions, refs, no
  secret, plain push to main).

# Reference consumer verification-and-review workflow, verified end to end in a
# fresh repository (GitHub-hosted runners, record-transport: job-output, provenance:
# summary). Save as .github/workflows/ci.yml. The bootstrap is referenced as
# gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main on purpose: the engine is resolved from protected
# main at run time, so a commit pin on the bootstrap adds little and only goes stale. Do not
# replace @main with a tag, another branch or a fork. The job named "verify" and its
# step names must match "verification" in .github/clouseau.json; adapt the install and
# test steps to your stack. Secrets (all optional, see docs/quickstart.md):
# DEEPSEEK_API_KEY, TYPESAFE_API_KEY, CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN.
name: CI
run-name: >-
  ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('Verify PR #{0}', github.event.pull_request.number) ||
      inputs.check_author && 'Verify repair author' ||
      format('PR review ({0})', github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref_name) }}
on:
  push:
    branches: ['policy-install/**']
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review]
  pull_request_target:
    branches: [main]
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, ready_for_review, edited]
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      pull_request:
        description: PR number to reassess without executing contributor code; empty runs verification
        type: string
        required: false
      check_author:
        description: Inspect existing repair author identity and repository access without writing or deploying
        type: boolean
        default: false
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.event.issue.number || inputs.pull_request || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  resolve-clouseau:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      sha: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.sha }}
      digest: ${{ steps.engine.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - id: engine
        uses: gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main
        with:
          provenance: summary

  # Optional: skip the checks a valid local receipt already attests (docs/local-review.md, "Receipt-attested verification").
  # Any other outcome, including an error here, leaves `attested` unset and `verify` runs every check.
  attested:
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
    outputs:
      attested: ${{ steps.decide.outputs.attested }}
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Decide whether a local receipt attests the verification
        id: decide
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        continue-on-error: true
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: attested
          config: .github/clouseau.json

  verify:
    # Schedule the job so GitHub resolves its name, including metadata events.
    # Step guards keep those events from running contributor code.
    name: >-
      ${{ (github.event_name == 'pull_request' ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)) && 'verify' || 'metadata-only' }}
    needs: [resolve-clouseau, attested]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        # `attested` is 'true' only for a pull request whose receipt attests this exact head; then every step is skipped and the
        # engine accepts the skipped required steps because it verifies the same receipt itself.
        if: &verify-code >-
          (github.event_name == 'pull_request' ||
          (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request == '' && !inputs.check_author)) &&
          needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *verify-code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Verify the frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: verify-engine
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        if: *verify-code
        with:
          node-version: '22'
      - name: Select accepted verification recipe
        if: *verify-code
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          if test -n "$BASE_SHA" && git cat-file -e "$BASE_SHA:.clouseau-local.json" 2>/dev/null; then
            git show "$BASE_SHA:.clouseau-local.json" > "$RUNNER_TEMP/clouseau-coverage.json"
          else
            cp .clouseau-local.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/clouseau-coverage.json"
          fi
      - name: Install verification dependencies
        if: *verify-code
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts
      - name: Run tests and measure native coverage
        if: *verify-code
        run: npm run test:coverage
      - name: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage
        if: *verify-code
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: coverage
          coverage-config: ${{ runner.temp }}/clouseau-coverage.json

  assess-intent:
    if: &review-event >-
      (github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
      (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.assessment || steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      review-record: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.review-record || steps.assess.outputs.review-record }}
      number: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
      # 'true' only when the receipt-only route found the receipt unusable; the only data that leaves this job towards assess-hosted
      hosted: ${{ steps.fallback.outputs.hosted }}
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Verify the owner-authorized frozen reviewer installation
        if: github.event_name == 'push'
        id: install
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            const match = context.ref.match(/^refs\/heads\/policy-install\/pr-([1-9][0-9]*)$/);
            if (context.actor !== context.repo.owner || !/^[a-f0-9]{40}$/.test(context.sha) || !match) {
              throw new Error('Reviewer installation requires the repository owner and a ready PR number');
            }
            const pull_number = Number(match[1]);
            if (!Number.isSafeInteger(pull_number)) throw new Error('Invalid installation PR number');
            const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number});
            if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.base.ref !== 'main' ||
                pr.user.login !== context.repo.owner || pr.head.sha !== context.sha ||
                pr.head.repo?.full_name !== `${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}`) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires the owner-authored same-repository PR at this exact workflow revision');
            }
            const comments = await github.paginate(github.rest.issues.listComments,
              {...context.repo, issue_number: pull_number, per_page: 100});
            if (!comments.some(comment => comment.user?.type === 'User' && comment.user.login === context.repo.owner &&
                comment.body.trim() === `/approve-intent ${context.sha}`)) {
              throw new Error('Installation requires owner intent confirmation at this exact revision');
            }
            core.setOutput('number', String(pull_number));
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Wait for tests and exact coverage
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          REQUESTED_PR: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
        with:
          script: |
            const path = require('node:path');
            const root = path.resolve('.clouseau-ci');
            const config = require(path.join(root, 'src/config.cjs')).loadConfig('.github/clouseau.json');
            const policy = require(path.join(root, 'src/policy.cjs')).createPolicy(config, {engine: require(path.join(root, 'src/central-version.cjs')).environmentEngine()});
            const number = context.payload.pull_request?.number || Number(process.env.REQUESTED_PR);
            for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 120; attempt++) {
              const {data: pr} = await github.rest.pulls.get({...context.repo, pull_number: number});
              const expected = context.payload.pull_request?.head.sha || context.sha;
              if (pr.state !== 'open' || pr.draft || pr.head.sha !== expected) {
                throw new Error('PR closed, became draft, or changed while verification was pending');
              }
              const result = await policy.technicalRun(github, context.repo, pr);
              if (result.failure) throw new Error(result.failure);
              if (!result.pending) { core.info(`Verified PR CI: ${result.url}. Clouseau acceptance can now start.`); return; }
              core.info('Waiting for independent verification and exact coverage. No AI request has been made.');
              await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 15000));
            }
            throw new Error('PR verification did not complete within 30 minutes');
      - name: Select authenticated local review or the installed CI reviewer
        id: review-route
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          script: |
            core.setOutput('local', String((context.payload.pull_request?.body || '').includes('clouseau-local-review:v1')));
      - name: Verify authenticated local review without AI credentials
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local == 'true'
        id: local-review
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: verify-local
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
      - name: Hand an unusable receipt to the separate hosted review
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local == 'true'
        id: fallback
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        env:
          ASSESSMENT: ${{ steps.local-review.outputs.assessment }}
        with:
          script: |
            const assessment = JSON.parse(process.env.ASSESSMENT);
            core.setOutput('hosted', String(assessment.decision === 'review_incomplete' && assessment.cause === 'local_receipt_unusable'));
      - name: Review unstamped PR through the installed CI AI reviewer
        if: steps.review-route.outputs.local != 'true'
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        id: assess
        with:
          operation: assess
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ steps.install.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}

  # Runs in this same workflow run only when the receipt-only job above found the receipt unusable. This is
  # the only job that holds the provider secrets for a PR that carries a receipt marker, and it never reads the
  # receipt (ignore-receipt) or any value derived from it: it receives just the PR number and the frozen engine.
  assess-hosted:
    if: needs.assess-intent.outputs.hosted == 'true'
    needs: [assess-intent, resolve-clouseau]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 70
    permissions:
      actions: read
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      issues: read
    outputs:
      assessment: ${{ steps.assess.outputs.assessment }}
      review-record: ${{ steps.assess.outputs.review-record }}
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      # Never load the controller or its configuration from the PR.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Review the change through the installed CI AI reviewer, ignoring the receipt
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        id: assess
        with:
          operation: assess
          ignore-receipt: 'true'
          record-transport: job-output
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          wait-for-verification: 'false'
          provider-key: ${{ secrets.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY }}
          typesafe-key: ${{ secrets.TYPESAFE_API_KEY }}

  approve-and-merge:
    name: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) || (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) && 'approve-and-merge' || 'metadata-only-approval' }}
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, resolve-clouseau]
    # Always resolve the job name; only trusted, ready PR events run its steps.
    # A failed assessment must still fail the required native approval check.
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number || github.run_id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - name: Require a completed assessment
        if: >-
          ((github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft) ||
          (github.event_name == 'push' && !github.event.deleted && startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/heads/policy-install/'))) &&
          (needs.assess-intent.result != 'success' || contains(fromJSON('["failure","cancelled"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result))
        run: exit 1
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        if: *review-event
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        if: *review-event
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - if: *review-event
        uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: gate
          record-transport: job-output
          # Exactly one acceptance record per head: the hosted review's when it ran, otherwise the receipt-only job's.
          review-record: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.review-record || needs.assess-intent.outputs.review-record }}
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          native-gate: 'true'
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  apply-repair:
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: >-
      always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request_target' && !github.event.pull_request.draft &&
      github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name == github.repository &&
      needs.assess-intent.result == 'success' && contains(fromJSON('["success","skipped"]'), needs.assess-hosted.result) &&
      needs.approve-and-merge.result == 'failure' &&
      fromJSON(needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment).repair_digest != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    permissions:
      contents: read
      issues: write
      pull-requests: read
      actions: read
    concurrency:
      group: pr-approval-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: repair
          record-transport: job-output
          review-record: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.review-record || needs.assess-intent.outputs.review-record }}
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}
          repair-token: ${{ secrets.CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN }}

  finalize-merge:
    needs: [assess-intent, assess-hosted, approve-and-merge, resolve-clouseau]
    if: *review-event
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: finalize
          pull-request: ${{ needs.assess-intent.outputs.number }}
          assessment: ${{ needs.assess-hosted.outputs.assessment || needs.assess-intent.outputs.assessment }}

  request-reassessment:
    if: >-
      (github.event_name == 'issue_comment' && github.event.issue.pull_request && (startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/approve-intent ') || startsWith(github.event.comment.body, '/hosted-review '))) ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.pull_request != '' && !inputs.check_author)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: read
      actions: write
    needs: resolve-clouseau
    env:
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_SHA: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha }}
      CLOUSEAU_ENGINE_DIGEST: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.digest }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          ref: main
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Check out this run frozen Clouseau engine
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          repository: gaulatti/clouseau
          ref: ${{ needs.resolve-clouseau.outputs.sha || '0000000000000000000000000000000000000000' }}
          path: .clouseau-ci
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.clouseau-ci
        with:
          operation: request-reassessment
          pull-request: ${{ inputs.pull_request }}

  check-author:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.check_author
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 3
    permissions: {}
    steps:
      - name: Verify independent repair author without writing
        uses: actions/github-script@v7
        with:
          github-token: ${{ secrets.CLOUSEAU_REPAIR_TOKEN }}
          script: |
            const {data: user} = await github.rest.users.getAuthenticated();
            const {data: repository} = await github.rest.repos.get(context.repo);
            if (user.login === 'github-actions[bot]' || !repository.permissions?.push) {
              throw new Error('Repair requires an independent author with Contents write access');
            }
            core.info(`Independent repair author ${user.login} can access ${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}. No write or deployment was made.`);

{
  "version": 1,
  "base_branch": "main",
  "workflow": "backend-ci.yml",
  "verification": {
    "job": "verify",
    "steps": [
      "Test approval policy",
      "Rust format and lint",
      "Run all targets with branch instrumentation",
      "Run documentation tests",
      "Verify container boundary",
      "Enforce 100% line and branch coverage"
    ]
  },
  "manual_reviewer": "gaulatti",
  "repository_policy": "test/fixtures/APPROVAL.md",
  "readme": "README.md",
  "sensitive_paths": [],
  "deployment": {
    "workflow": "backend-deploy.yml",
    "paths": [
      "src/",
      "migrations/",
      "vendor/",
      "scripts/",
      "tests/",
      "Cargo.toml",
      "Cargo.lock",
      "Dockerfile",
      ".dockerignore",
      "compose.yaml",
      ".github/workflows/backend-deploy.yml"
    ]
  }
}

claims.title: ci(verify): keep the self-tests in verify so main's gate can judge this change
claims.description:
Split Clouseau's own CI so that a valid local receipt skips only the receipt-covered verification steps, and the engine's self-tests always run.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add an `attested` job, as in examples/consumer-ci.yml. It runs the frozen engine's `operation: attested` on the base revision, never pull request code, with continue-on-error. `verify` keeps exactly the receipt-covered steps: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage, Test approval policy, Test distributable action without Git metadata, Test workflow security. It skips them only when `attested` is 'true'. The five coverage-contract self-tests stay in `verify` under a condition that never reads the receipt decision (main's gate reads main's configuration, which requires them in `verify`; a separate job would fail this PR's own run). Beside them, `verify` also runs `node scripts/review-compatibility verify` on the merge ref, because under binding "diff" a receipt compares compatibility declarations by meaning, so the declaration-to-tree check must run outside the receipt.
- `.github/clouseau.json`: `verification.steps` lists only the four receipt-covered steps. No new configuration key: the gate's technical check already requires the whole verification run to conclude success, so a failed self-test blocks approval though the configuration does not list it.
- Integrator flag: set `hosted_review: "manual"` (its code is on main). The reassessment trigger also starts on `/hosted-review ` comments, as the docs require for a consumer that sets it.
- Prove that an unattested PR still runs every step, that a skipped required step without a valid attesting receipt is still a failure (the existing policy test), and that a failed self-test is a technical failure whatever a receipt says. The attested job is continue-on-error at job level, and assess-installation guards on explicit needs results because verify's needs are skipped on an installation push.
- Document the pattern in docs/local-review.md.

report.summary: Clouseau's CI gains a read-only, continue-on-error attested job (frozen engine, base revision) whose output lets a valid receipt skip only the four configured verify steps; the coverage-contract self-tests and a new review-compatibility verify step run under a guard that never reads attested, and the gate's run-conclusion check fails the PR if they fail. Configuration lists the four steps and sets hosted_review manual with its /hosted-review trigger; assess-installation uses explicit needs results. Tests evaluate real expressions and the real gate. Only a low-score comment inaccuracy about coverage.py setup was found.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

```yaml
if: needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'   # on each test step, or on a whole job in another workflow
```

The skip is advisory; the enforcement is in the engine. When the configured `verification.job` succeeds with required steps `skipped`,
the engine accepts them only after verifying the same receipt itself in the trusted workflow; without a valid attesting receipt a skipped
required step is the failure it always was. A receipt expires (`max_age_seconds`), so re-run the workflow after expiry and the checks run;
the failure then names the receipt class (`receipt_expired` with its expiry instant) and that step, or `clouseau refresh --pr N` to renew
the receipt ([notices](notices.md#skipped-verification-step-without-an-attesting-receipt)).
The job named in `verification.job` must still exist and succeed, so keep it as a job whose steps are skipped rather than removing it.

A check that no receipt may stand in for stays in the workflow without an `attested` condition, and the configuration does
not list it. It may sit in `verification.job` itself or in another job of the same workflow. The gate requires the whole
verification run to conclude `success`, not only the listed steps, so its failure blocks approval like a failure of a
required step, and it needs no configuration key. In Clouseau's own CI, `verify` holds both kinds of step. The four
receipt-covered steps listed in `.github/clouseau.json` take the `attested` condition. Under a condition that never reads it
are the coverage-contract self-tests, which test the engine's coverage gate rather than the change, and
`scripts/review-compatibility verify`, which checks the review-semantics declarations against the merged tree. The
declaration check must stay outside the receipt: under `binding: "diff"` a receipt compares declarations by what they
declare, not by their digests ([receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)).

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (in the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file. A receipt that attests
the verification skips that suite, so Clouseau's CI also runs `scripts/review-compatibility verify` in `verify` under a
condition no receipt changes, against the tree the run verifies:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.

Two more classes are only ever shown when no receipt can be used at all:
`absent` (the description carries no marker) and `unread` (a hosted fallback run
does not read receipts). Repositories in `required` mode have no hosted review to
fall back to. The notice then says `This repository requires a valid receipt, so
nothing is approved until you do the following.` and the outcome is
`local_receipt_required`; no provider call is made. On the receipt-only route
(`local_receipt_unusable`) the reason itself carries the cause sentence. While tests are pending or failing, an ignored receipt behaves exactly like
an unstamped change (the pending or blocked result carries the notice).

#### Manual hosted review (opt-in)

The protected top-level `hosted_review` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch says whether the CI AI review of a pull
request with no usable receipt starts by itself:

| `hosted_review` | No usable receipt (absent, expired or otherwise unusable) |
| --- | --- |
| absent or `"automatic"` | today's behavior: the CI AI review runs (optional mode), or `local_receipt_required` (required mode) |
| `"manual"` | `review_incomplete`, cause `hosted_review_manual`, no provider call, until a maintainer requests the review |

The request reaches the engine only through the repository workflow: its `issue_comment` condition must start a run for
`/hosted-review ` comments, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does. The engine never sees a comment that starts no run, so it
cannot detect a workflow without that trigger; the hold notice therefore names the missing condition as its last step. A
consumer that sets `hosted_review: "manual"` adds the condition in the same change.

The request is a comment `/hosted-review <head sha>` on the pull request, validated as `/approve-intent` is: the exact current
head, a real user (not a bot), write permission or higher, and re-read by the engine itself from the pull request's comments.
How the run was started never matters, only such a comment. With a valid request the run proceeds as `"automatic"` would; a
request for an older head, from a reader or from a bot is ignored. A valid receipt is used whatever the setting, and a
repository in `required` mode keeps `local_receipt_required`. The receipt-only job still holds no provider secret: in manual
mode it returns `local_receipt_unusable` only when a valid request exists, so the reference workflow's hosted fallback below

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.

Split Clouseau's own CI so that a valid local receipt skips only the receipt-covered verification steps, and the engine's self-tests always run.

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add an `attested` job, as in examples/consumer-ci.yml. It runs the frozen engine's `operation: attested` on the base revision, never pull request code, with continue-on-error. `verify` keeps exactly the receipt-covered steps: Enforce 100% line and branch coverage, Test approval policy, Test distributable action without Git metadata, Test workflow security. It skips them only when `attested` is 'true'. The five coverage-contract self-tests stay in `verify` under a condition that never reads the receipt decision (main's gate reads main's configuration, which requires them in `verify`; a separate job would fail this PR's own run). Beside them, `verify` also runs `node scripts/review-compatibility verify` on the merge ref, because under binding "diff" a receipt compares compatibility declarations by meaning, so the declaration-to-tree check must run outside the receipt.
- `.github/clouseau.json`: `verification.steps` lists only the four receipt-covered steps. No new configuration key: the gate's technical check already requires the whole verification run to conclude success, so a failed self-test blocks approval though the configuration does not list it.
- Integrator flag: set `hosted_review: "manual"` (its code is on main). The reassessment trigger also starts on `/hosted-review ` comments, as the docs require for a consumer that sets it.
- Prove that an unattested PR still runs every step, that a skipped required step without a valid attesting receipt is still a failure (the existing policy test), and that a failed self-test is a technical failure whatever a receipt says. The attested job is continue-on-error at job level, and assess-installation guards on explicit needs results because verify's needs are skipped on an installation push.
- Document the pattern in docs/local-review.md.

# Receipt compatibility across engine revisions

A signed local review receipt names the engine revision that produced it (`reviewer_sha`, `reviewer_digest`). Today CI
accepts it only when that is exactly the protected `main` it resolved. `main` moves many times a day, so a receipt
rots within hours and CI repeats a review (about $6 and several minutes) even when the engine change cannot affect what
the review attests. This design lets CI accept a receipt issued under revision X while running revision Y, if and only if
Y itself declares X's review semantics compatible. If CI cannot establish that, it behaves as it does today: the receipt is
ignored and CI reviews.

## Design

**Review-semantics digest.** `src/review-semantics.cjs` hashes every engine file under the same roots as the exact engine
digest (`action.yml`, `src`, `policy`, `bin`, `skills`, `scripts`; tests excluded) *except* the files listed in its
`NEUTRAL` table. Each neutral file has a written reason. A file is semantic by default: a new or renamed file is part of
the meaning until a person lists it as neutral. The table lives in `review-semantics.cjs`, which is itself semantic, so
moving a file into it changes the digest and forces the same decision as editing the file would.

**Compatibility statement.** `policy/review-compatibility.json` is in-tree on protected main:

```json
{"version": 1, "current": "<digest of this tree>", "compatible": ["<older digest>", "..."]}
```

`current` must equal the digest of the tree that contains it. `compatible` lists earlier semantics whose receipts this
tree accepts (at most 64, newest first, never including `current`). The statement is the only source of compatibility.

Two further files exist only to keep the statement in step with the tree, and `acceptor()` never reads them:

- `compat/manifest.json` lists the semantic files (path, executable bits, content hash) the statement was last folded for.
  Its digest must equal `current`. It lets a tool say which semantic files changed since the fold by comparing two file
  lists, with no Git history.
- `compat/declarations/<digest>.json`, one file per pull request, state that a set of semantic files changed (by content
  hash, or deleted) and whether the change is `compatible` or `incompatible`. A declaration is inert until it is folded.

**Receipt.** A receipt additionally signs `reviewer_semantics`, the digest of the engine that issued it. Receipts without
the field behave exactly as before.

**Acceptance.** `verifySignedRecord` keeps every check it has (enrolled key, author, expiry, record binding, repository,
head, base, policy and configuration digests, recomputed decision, passing result). Only when the exact engine comparison
fails, and only in central-source mode, it asks `acceptor()` whether the receipt's `reviewer_semantics` is acceptable.

`acceptor()` reads the statement from the engine checkout that is running, the checkout `identifyEngine` and
`verifyEngine` already bound to the SHA the resolver read from protected `gaulatti/clouseau` `main`. It answers yes only
if the statement parses, `current` equals the digest it computes from that checkout, and the claim is `current` or listed.
Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

```yaml
if: needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'   # on each test step, or on a whole job in another workflow
```

The skip is advisory; the enforcement is in the engine. When the configured `verification.job` succeeds with required steps `skipped`,
the engine accepts them only after verifying the same receipt itself in the trusted workflow; without a valid attesting receipt a skipped
required step is the failure it always was. A receipt expires (`max_age_seconds`), so re-run the workflow after expiry and the checks run;
the failure then names the receipt class (`receipt_expired` with its expiry instant) and that step, or `clouseau refresh --pr N` to renew
the receipt ([notices](notices.md#skipped-verification-step-without-an-attesting-receipt)).
The job named in `verification.job` must still exist and succeed, so keep it as a job whose steps are skipped rather than removing it.

A check that no receipt may stand in for stays in the workflow without an `attested` condition, and the configuration does
not list it. It may sit in `verification.job` itself or in another job of the same workflow. The gate requires the whole
verification run to conclude `success`, not only the listed steps, so its failure blocks approval like a failure of a
required step, and it needs no configuration key. In Clouseau's own CI, `verify` holds both kinds of step. The four
receipt-covered steps listed in `.github/clouseau.json` take the `attested` condition. Under a condition that never reads it
are the coverage-contract self-tests, which test the engine's coverage gate rather than the change, and
`scripts/review-compatibility verify`, which checks the review-semantics declarations against the merged tree. The
declaration check must stay outside the receipt: under `binding: "diff"` a receipt compares declarations by what they
declare, not by their digests ([receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)).

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.

`acceptor()` reads the statement from the engine checkout that is running, the checkout `identifyEngine` and
`verifyEngine` already bound to the SHA the resolver read from protected `gaulatti/clouseau` `main`. It answers yes only
if the statement parses, `current` equals the digest it computes from that checkout, and the claim is `current` or listed.
Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (in the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file. A receipt that attests
the verification skips that suite, so Clouseau's CI also runs `scripts/review-compatibility verify` in `verify` under a
condition no receipt changes, against the tree the run verifies:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.

# Clouseau review contract

Clouseau provides shared, evidence-bound repository change assessment, exact
coverage gates, native PR approval and merge, and deployment-driven wiki updates.
Consumers provide their own protected purpose contract and verification steps.

Local agent review and authenticated receipt reuse serve the same change
acceptance purpose. Agent-only installation and refresh are independent of CI
installation. A protected verifier may reuse an enrolled runner's source-bound
passing review without another AI request, while preserving native tests, exact
coverage, existing owner authority and branch protection. Initial workstation
signing explicitly trusts the enrolled operator and privileged processes; it
does not claim hardware attestation or protection from a compromised runner.

Changes must preserve the trust boundary between untrusted contributor source,
secret-free execution checks, read-only AI evaluation and the separate write
controller. Native protected-main requirements, immutable revision identities,
meaningful tests and exact 100% line and branch coverage are mandatory.
Model text is data. It must never execute as a command or grant permissions.

An explicitly accepted manual-only integration must enforce branch protection
where GitHub makes it available and disable automatic merge for every author.
GitHub's documented private-plan protection limitation may permit independent
review and approval without host-enforced merge blocking, but never automatic
merge, waived tests, lowered coverage or omitted current-head owner approval for
external contributions. Missing credentials or generic API failures are not
evidence of that plan limitation. Report the enforcement boundary truthfully.

Useful defect repairs, meaningful tests, provider qualification and maintenance
serve this purpose without a new product decision. Speculative frameworks,
unrelated capabilities or additional authority require concrete justification.
The shared protocol defines product and technical scoring; no owner intent
confirmation waives integrity failures, incomplete evidence or technical defects.

Changes to the reviewer implementation, scoring policy, verification controls or
this purpose contract require explicit exact-revision confirmation from gaulatti.
Only real purpose, authority and outcome tradeoffs are sent to the owner. A
missing provider response or unresolved code concern belongs to automated
investigation or bounded repair, never automatic approval.
