Declare every check you want skipped in CI (tests, coverage, fmt, lint, frontend, infrastructure) as a command of `.clouseau-local.json`.
Without an enrolled identity nothing is signed and the review remains advisory. The signed verification record then carries
`attestation: {version, recipe, commands, coverage_mode, gate: "passed"}`; receipts issued before this change carry none, stay valid for the
AI review, and attest no verification.

In CI, `operation: attested` (inputs `config`, `github-token`; output `attested`) answers `'true'` only when the pull request's receipt passes
every check the assessment applies (signature, enrolled key and author, expiry, exact head and base, engine, signed sources against live
GitHub; under the protected `binding: "diff"` the normalized diff and the live base's recipe instead of the head, base and sources, see
[binding a receipt to its diff](#binding-a-receipt-to-its-diff-opt-in)) AND attests the accepted base recipe. Anything else (no marker,
expired, wrong head without that binding, old receipt, an error) is `'false'`. Gate any
workflow on it in a small job, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does:

```yaml
if: needs.attested.outputs.attested != 'true'   # on each test step, or on a whole job in another workflow
```

The skip is advisory; the enforcement is in the engine. When the configured `verification.job` succeeds with required steps `skipped`,
the engine accepts them only after verifying the same receipt itself in the trusted workflow; without a valid attesting receipt a skipped
required step is the failure it always was. A receipt expires (`max_age_seconds`), so re-run the workflow after expiry and the checks run;
the failure then names the receipt class (`receipt_expired` with its expiry instant) and that step, or `clouseau refresh --pr N` to renew
the receipt ([notices](notices.md#skipped-verification-step-without-an-attesting-receipt)).
The job named in `verification.job` must still exist and succeed, so keep it as a job whose steps are skipped rather than removing it.

A check that no receipt may stand in for stays in the workflow without an `attested` condition, and the configuration does
not list it. It may sit in `verification.job` itself or in another job of the same workflow. The gate requires the whole
verification run to conclude `success`, not only the listed steps, so its failure blocks approval like a failure of a
required step, and it needs no configuration key. In Clouseau's own CI, `verify` holds both kinds of step. The four
receipt-covered steps listed in `.github/clouseau.json` take the `attested` condition. Under a condition that never reads it
are the coverage-contract self-tests, which test the engine's coverage gate rather than the change, and
`scripts/review-compatibility verify`, which checks the review-semantics declarations against the merged tree. The
declaration check must stay outside the receipt: under `binding: "diff"` a receipt compares declarations by what they
declare, not by their digests ([receipt compatibility](receipt-compatibility.md)).

## Evidence size

The review cache's `snapshot.json`, the `record` output and the signed `receipt.json` are
written as compact JSON, without indentation (about 15% of a typical receipt); they parse
identically and the published artifact was already compact.

`acceptor()` reads the statement from the engine checkout that is running, the checkout `identifyEngine` and
`verifyEngine` already bound to the SHA the resolver read from protected `gaulatti/clouseau` `main`. It answers yes only
if the statement parses, `current` equals the digest it computes from that checkout, and the claim is `current` or listed.
Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (in the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file. A receipt that attests
the verification skips that suite, so Clouseau's CI also runs `scripts/review-compatibility verify` in `verify` under a
condition no receipt changes, against the tree the run verifies:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails

# Clouseau

Clouseau also provides a centrally maintained local agent skill and signed review
receipts. Agent-only installation is independent of CI: it uses authenticated
coding harnesses and creates no Actions configuration or provider secrets.
Inside Claude Code, Codex or opencode the calling agent supplies the review
sessions (`--agent`); the headless `--harness` form is for a plain terminal.
Local AI review runs regardless of coverage percentage or availability and keeps
its quality verdict separate from real verification results. Opted-in CI verifies
an enrolled runner's passing AI receipt without repeating the review, then still
requires its own tests and exact coverage before approval/merge. See
[local review, installation and trust boundaries](docs/local-review.md).
New to Clouseau? Start with the [quickstart](docs/quickstart.md).
How a receipt stays valid across engine revisions: [receipt compatibility](docs/receipt-compatibility.md).
Every refusal or hold notice names its cause class and numbered next steps: [notices and their causes](docs/notices.md).
Consumers without accepted recipe/enrollment/workflows use the separate
[initial owner-authorized trust installation](docs/initial-installation.md).
Its signed evidence cannot approve ordinary changes or automatically merge.
Clouseau's own accepted-policy bootstrap and native coverage diagnostics are
documented in [self-review](docs/self-review.md).

Shared coverage gates and evidence-led AI pull request approval for GitHub Actions.
Clouseau owns the PR intent review process: check whether a change is needed,
compare it with repository contracts and precedent, request the owner's second
opinion when necessary, and approve and arm auto-merge only after every technical
requirement passes. The initial implementation was extracted from Colombo.

Version 2 implements the [change acceptance protocol](docs/change-acceptance.md):
product fit, need and proportionality; nine-factor technical findings; independent
source investigations; a persistent evidence ledger; bounded repairs; and native
protected auto-merge. Humans decide genuine purpose and authority questions.
Technical uncertainty goes to automated investigation and cannot be waived by
an intent comment. Version 1 remains explicit compatibility for existing pins.

## Ownership

Clouseau contains the coverage checker, regression tests, PR intent review rules,
DeepSeek integration, approval controller, and reusable composite action.
Each consuming repository keeps its build/test commands, a configuration file,
and its own purpose, contracts, acceptance criteria, and manual-review owner.

`request-reassessment` with actions write and contents/pull-requests read access;
they rerun the current revision's existing `pull_request_target` run. Its test job
is skipped, so confirming intent does not rebuild the container. The handler
validates maintainer permission and exact comment SHA before requesting a rerun.

Run `finalize` in a separate job after the native gate succeeds, with actions
write and contents/pull-requests read access and no provider key. Auto-merge must
wait for the required gate job to finish, so deployment handoff cannot run inside
that gate. A provider diagnostic remains read-only and never approves a PR.

`deployment` is either `null` or an explicit workflow and path list. For a bot
merge touching those paths, Clouseau dispatches that existing workflow because
`GITHUB_TOKEN` merges suppress push-triggered workflows. It verifies main still
points at the merged revision. Deployment health, staged rollout, smoke tests,
bake windows, and ticket closure remain separate delivery work.

## Development

```sh
node --test src/*.test.cjs
```

Clouseau's own CI also requires exactly 100% line and branch coverage across
all production JavaScript modules. New source files are included
even when no test imports them. Test code is outside the production scope;
there are no exclusions for production failure paths or rounded thresholds.

To run the same gate locally with Node 22:

```sh
./scripts/verify-coverage
```

Clouseau needs only Node. One integration test runs a fixture Python application
under real coverage.py to prove the `coveragepy` adapter against live output, so
install `requirements-test.txt` (coverage.py 7.13.0) to run the whole suite. The
coverage gate itself is `bin/coverage-gate.cjs`
(`check REPORT SOURCE_DIRECTORY [llvm|istanbul|coveragepy|go]` or
`plan ACCEPTED_CONFIG [DIRECTORY]`), so reviewing a Python application requires
Python only for that application's own tests.

Post-deployment wiki maintenance is a separate, already supported operation.
Source merge, deployment, live health and published documentation remain distinct
results; do not infer one from another.

Serialized local evidence is capped at 900,000 characters. To keep large changes inside the cap
without dropping anything a reviewer judges, the local collector stores a file added whole once:
its snapshot entry keeps the patch header and `patch_body: "head_source"`, the body being exactly
the head source with every line prefixed `+` (consumers restore the identical patch). The pinned
engine seed (roughly 380 KB) is collected only when a workflow change adds or changes a
`gaulatti/clouseau/scripts/resolve@main` (or an existing `@<sha>`) reference; an ordinary edit of a workflow that keeps its reference
carries no engine source, and a reviewer can still request any of it. The seed is optional context: seed files that would use the last 150,000
characters are listed in `omitted_sources` with a reason, and reviewers can still request them.
Changed files, their base and head sources and contracts are never omitted; a change that exceeds

| `revision_head` | Issued for a different head (both short ids are named) |
| `revision_base` | Issued against a base that has since moved (both short ids are named; step: `gh pr update-branch N`) |
| `changed` | The protected policy or configuration changed after issue (which one is named) |
| `source` | Signed sources, file inventory or diff differ from the pull request (including a changed lockfile summary) |
| `record` | The record, its digest, history, chunked structure or claimed decision is inconsistent or incomplete |
| `engine` | Produced by a different engine revision than the protected one (both short ids are named) |
| `not_passing` | The review it records did not pass |
| `settings` | The protected chunked review configuration is invalid, so the receipt cannot be checked |
| `untested`, `integrity`, `completeness` | Its evidence does not meet hosted approval's affirmative-evidence rule; the rule and, where it applies, the files are named |

Two more classes are only ever shown when no receipt can be used at all:
`absent` (the description carries no marker) and `unread` (a hosted fallback run
does not read receipts). Repositories in `required` mode have no hosted review to
fall back to. The notice then says `This repository requires a valid receipt, so
nothing is approved until you do the following.` and the outcome is
`local_receipt_required`; no provider call is made. On the receipt-only route
(`local_receipt_unusable`) the reason itself carries the cause sentence. While tests are pending or failing, an ignored receipt behaves exactly like
an unstamped change (the pending or blocked result carries the notice).

#### Manual hosted review (opt-in)

The protected top-level `hosted_review` in `.github/clouseau.json` on the base branch says whether the CI AI review of a pull
request with no usable receipt starts by itself:

| `hosted_review` | No usable receipt (absent, expired or otherwise unusable) |
| --- | --- |
| absent or `"automatic"` | today's behavior: the CI AI review runs (optional mode), or `local_receipt_required` (required mode) |
| `"manual"` | `review_incomplete`, cause `hosted_review_manual`, no provider call, until a maintainer requests the review |

The request reaches the engine only through the repository workflow: its `issue_comment` condition must start a run for
`/hosted-review ` comments, as `examples/consumer-ci.yml` does. The engine never sees a comment that starts no run, so it

#### Hosted review after an unusable receipt (reference consumer workflow)

A workflow that routes a PR whose description carries a receipt marker to a
`verify-local` job holds no provider credential in that job: the secret must not
be exposed to a job that runs on a contributor-supplied receipt. When that job finds
an optional-mode receipt unusable (decision `review_incomplete`, cause
`local_receipt_unusable`) the same run continues in a separate `assess-hosted` job
that holds the provider secrets. It runs `assess` with `ignore-receipt: 'true'`, so
the receipt is never read there, and it receives only the PR number and the frozen
engine, never an assessment, notice or record from the receipt-only job. Its
assessment and review record replace the receipt-only job's in `approve-and-merge`,
`apply-repair` and `finalize-merge`, so exactly one acceptance record is consumed per
head. A valid receipt skips the job entirely and no provider call is made. A
repository in `required` mode reports `local_receipt_required` and has no fallback.
The "receipt not used" notice is not shown on the fallback path because the
hosted job deliberately does not know why the receipt was unusable; the receipt-only
job log still carries the warning annotation naming the cause. The owner no longer
needs to remove the marker to obtain the CI review.

### Protected files make a receipt unusable in CI

A change to any protected control path (the CI workflow, `.github/ci/`,
`.github/clouseau.json`, CODEOWNERS, `.clouseau-local.json`, the repository
policy file, `AGENTS.md`, and the configured `sensitive_paths`) needs exact-head

Everything else answers no.

## Declare, then fold

A pull request never rewrites the statement. Two pull requests that each change semantic files therefore never touch the
same line, and merge in either order without a manual re-bump.

**In the pull request.** When semantic files change, `src/review-semantics.test.cjs` (the required `verify` job) fails with
"Undeclared review-semantics change" until the author records the decision, which adds one new file:

- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --compatible`: the change cannot alter what a review attests (refactor, comment,
  performance, a notice). Earlier receipts stay acceptable.
- `scripts/review-compatibility declare --incompatible`: the change alters rubrics, prompts, schema, scoring, validation,
  source selection, receipt format or anything else a review means. Every earlier receipt is ignored and CI reviews, which
  is the safe default for doubt.

The declaration names each changed semantic file with its content hash (a deleted file as `sha256: null`). The file is named
by the digest of its own content. `verify` passes only when every changed semantic file is covered by exactly one
declaration whose hash equals the file in the tree, and every declaration covers a file that really changed. An undeclared
change, a declaration for a file that did not change, a file changed again after it was declared, two declarations for one
file, an unknown file in `compat/declarations/` and a manifest that does not match the statement all fail `verify`.

**On protected main.** `scripts/review-compatibility fold` turns the declarations into the new statement and manifest and
deletes them. It runs only in `.github/workflows/compat-fold.yml`, which checks out `main` alone, and the command itself
refuses unless `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is `gaulatti/clouseau` and `GITHUB_REF` is `refs/heads/main`. It validates exactly as
`verify` does and changes nothing on any inconsistency. If every declaration is `compatible`, the previous `current` moves
into `compatible`; if any is `incompatible`, `compatible` is emptied. It is deterministic (same tree, same bytes),
idempotent (a second run finds nothing to fold) and its result passes `scripts/review-compatibility check`. The workflow
then runs `check` and the engine tests again before pushing one plain, fast-forward commit; if `main` moved it folds again
from the new `main`.

`scripts/review-compatibility check` succeeds only on a folded tree. `verify` also succeeds on a tree that carries
valid, not yet folded declarations. `scripts/review-compatibility bump --compatible|--incompatible` remains as the manual
equivalent of a fold for a maintainer repairing a tree by hand: it applies the decision to everything that changed, rewrites
statement and manifest together and consumes the declarations. A pull request that still edits the statement by hand fails
`verify` unless it also keeps manifest and declarations consistent, and costs the conflicts this design removes, so use
`declare`.

    name: >-
